title: Find Kth Character in Expanded String
summary: Given a string s with words separated by spaces, where each word contains only lowercase letters, create a new string t by repeating each character in a word according to its position.
statement: Given a string s with words separated by spaces, where each word contains only lowercase letters, create a new string t by repeating each character in a word according to its position. For example, 'hello' becomes 'heelllllllooooo'. Given an integer k, return the k-th character of the expanded string t.
constraints: s contains lowercase words separated by single spaces and has no leading or trailing space.
Within each word, character i is repeated i+1 times; original spaces remain single.
k is a valid zero-based index in the expanded string.
hints: A word of length m expands to triangular length m(m+1)/2.
Skip whole expanded words and their single separators until k lies inside one word.
Within that word, accumulate block sizes one, two, and so on until the block containing k is reached.
The skipped lengths exactly partition the expanded string, so the first containing block identifies the requested character without constructing t.
editorial: The skipped lengths exactly partition the expanded string, so the first containing block identifies the requested character without constructing t.

tests.explanation: The first expanded character is h.
The first expanded word has length fifteen, so index fifteen is the separating space.
